    body:
        sidebar:
            A sidebar along the left of the body displays a tree view of the
            current @{ProjectDirectoryScope}. Folders are listed before files,
            both by name, and a folder's contents are shown when it is
            expanded. The tree refreshes by itself when files or folders are
            added, removed, or renamed on disk, keeping expanded folders open
            and the selection in place. The sidebar is resized by dragging its
            edge. Until a project is picked it reads "No project open".

        gitStatus:
            When the project is inside a git repository, the tree colors each
            name by its git status: modified, added, untracked, and conflicted
            each have their own color, and ignored files and folders are
            dimmed. Unchanged names keep the default color. A folder takes the
            color of the most pressing status among its contents, conflicted
            first, then modified, added, and untracked, so a change stays
            visible while its folder is collapsed. The colors suit both the
            light and the dark theme. The highlighting refreshes by itself when
            files change on disk or the repository's state changes, such as
            after staging, committing, or switching branches. Outside a git
            repository the tree is not highlighted.

        openFile:
            Clicking a file in the tree opens it in an @{EditorScope}, in a
            split beside the chat history: the file on the left taking 50% of
            the width, the chat history on the right taking the rest. The split
            can be resized by dragging its edge. Closing the file closes the
            split. The @{ChatInputScope} is never split: it stays along the
            bottom, across the full width of prompt mode.

        promptMode:
            The body displays the @{PromptEditor} and any splits, to the
            right of the sidebar.

    shape: {FileTreeShape}

    description:
        Folders are listed before files, both by name, and a folder's contents
        are shown when it is expanded. Until a project is picked it reads

        place.

        names keep the default color. A folder takes the color of the most
        pressing status among its contents, conflicted first, then modified,
        added, and untracked, so a change stays visible while its folder is
        collapsed. The colors suit both the light and the dark theme. The
        highlighting refreshes by itself when files change on disk or the
        repository's state changes, such as after staging, committing, or
        switching branches. Outside a git repository the tree is not
        highlighted.

    opening:

        tree.

content.text:
The file tree now has its own scope, `FileTreeScope` in `spec/ui/components/file-tree/index.pi`, next to the ribbon and history list. Everywhere that described it or mentioned "the project tree" now references it. `piton check` and `piton build check` pass. I didn't touch `src/`.

**What moved into `FileTreeScope`:**
- **Layout:** folders before files, sorted by name; folders expand to show their contents; "No project open" until a project is picked.
- **Refreshing:** it updates itself when files change on disk, keeping expanded folders and the selection.
- **Git status:** the whole colouring section, unchanged.
- **Opening:** clicking a file opens it, and the scope leaves where it opens up to whatever holds the tree.

**What changed where it's used:**
- **`MainWindow.pi`:** the sidebar now just holds the `FileTreeScope` and can be resized by dragging. The separate git status section is gone from here. The open-file section still describes the 50% editor split, now starting "A file clicked in the `FileTreeScope`…".
- **`editor/index.pi`:** the pitch says the editor is for a file opened from the `FileTreeScope`.
- **`palette/index.pi`:** picking a file opens it "as clicking it in the `FileTreeScope` does".

Sidebar resizing stayed in `MainWindow`, since that's the sidebar rather than the tree. The generated `.claude/reference` docs won't have the new page until you run `piton build`.
